questions.question_text: Diameter of a circle with compass radius set to 4.5 cm is:
Circles sharing the exact same center point but different radii are called:
Write 3-step instructions to construct a circle of radius 3.5 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Mark center O. 2. Set compass span 3.5 cm against ruler. 3. Fix needle at O and rotate pencil 360°.

questions.question_text: Which tool is best suited for transferring exact segment lengths accurately?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Compass (or Divider).

questions.question_text: Construct a rectangle ABCD with AB = 6 cm and BC = 4 cm using ruler and set-square.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Draw AB = 6 cm. Use set-square at A and B to draw 90° rays. Mark AD = 4 cm, BC = 4 cm. Join C and D.

questions.question_text: Explain why a compass is superior to a marked ruler for copying segment lengths.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A compass locks an exact physical distance between its points, eliminating visual estimation and tick mark reading errors.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Inscribing Regular Hexagon. A student draws a circle of radius 4 cm.
(a) How can the student construct a regular hexagon inside this circle using compass radius steps? (2 marks)
(b) Calculate perimeter of the inscribed regular hexagon. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Keep compass span 4 cm. Mark consecutive 4 cm arcs around circle boundary. The 6 intersection points form vertices of regular hexagon.
(b) Side length = 4 cm. Perimeter = 6 x 4 = 24 cm.

questions.question_text: Radius of a circle of diameter 14 cm is:
Angle between set-square edges used for drawing perpendiculars is:
Construct two concentric circles of radii 3 cm and 5 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Mark center O. Draw first circle with 3 cm radius. Keep needle at O, set compass to 5 cm, draw second circle.

questions.question_text: Find distance between centers of two touching circles of radii 4 cm and 6 cm (touching externally).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Distance = r1 + r2 = 4 + 6 = 10 cm.

questions.question_text: Construct a square PQRS of side 5 cm using ruler and set-square.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Draw PQ = 5 cm. Draw perpendiculars at P and Q using set-square. Mark PS = 5 cm, QR = 5 cm. Join S and R.

questions.question_text: State the geometric definition of a circle in terms of set of points.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A circle is the set of all points in a plane that are at a fixed distance (radius r) from a fixed reference point (center O).

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Concentric Archery Target. An archery target consists of 3 concentric circles centered at O with radii 5 cm, 10 cm, and 15 cm.
(a) Find area of the innermost central circle (radius 5 cm). Use pi = 3.14. (2 marks)
(b) Find area of middle ring band between radius 5 cm and 10 cm. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Innermost Area = pi x r1^2 = 3.14 x 25 = 78.5 sq cm.
(b) Outer Circle Area (r=10) = 3.14 x 100 = 314 sq cm. Middle Ring Area = 314 - 78.5 = 235.5 sq cm.

questions.question_text: How many endpoints does a radius line segment of a circle have?
Longest chord of a circle is its:
Draw line segment AB = 7 cm and construct its perpendicular bisector.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Draw AB = 7 cm. Open compass > 3.5 cm. Draw arcs above/below from A and B. Join arc intersections.

questions.question_text: Can a triangle have side lengths 3 cm, 4 cm, and 8 cm? Construct or explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No! Sum of any two sides must be greater than third side: 3 + 4 = 7 < 8. Construction fails.

questions.question_text: Construct an isosceles triangle ABC with base BC = 6 cm and equal sides AB = AC = 5 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Draw BC = 6 cm. Set compass to 5 cm. Draw arcs from B and C to intersect at A. Join AB and AC.

questions.question_text: Explain step-by-step how to construct a right-angled triangle with legs 3 cm and 4 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Draw base BC = 4 cm. At B, draw 90° ray using set-square. Mark BA = 3 cm on ray. Join AC.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Circle Partition by Chords. A circle of radius 6 cm is drawn with diameter AB.
(a) State length of diameter AB and locate center O. (2 marks)
(b) Construct perpendicular diameter CD to AB and name the 4 right angles formed at center O. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Diameter AB = 2 x 6 = 12 cm. Center O is midpoint of AB (6 cm from A and B).
(b) Perpendicular diameter CD meets AB at 90° at O. 4 central right angles: AOC, COB, BOD, DOA (90° each).

questions.question_text: Instrument used to draw smooth arcs and circles is:
If radius of a circle is 8.5 cm, its diameter is:
Construct angle of 90° at point P on line l using set-square.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Align set-square baseline with l at P. Draw ray along vertical edge.

questions.question_text: Find distance between center points of two concentric circles.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Distance is ZERO because concentric circles share the exact same center point.

questions.question_text: Construct a square inside a circle of radius 4 cm such that square vertices lie on circle boundary.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Draw circle r=4. Draw two perpendicular diameters AC and BD. Join A-B-C-D to form inscribed square.

questions.question_text: State difference between set-squares found in a standard geometry box (45°-45°-90° vs 30°-60°-90°).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 45°-45°-90° set-square is isosceles right triangle. 30°-60°-90° set-square is scalene right triangle.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Geometric Design of Flower Petals. A 6-petal flower motif is constructed inside a 5 cm circle.
(a) Describe how petal arcs are drawn using radius step transfers. (2 marks)
(b) Prove that all petal tips lie on the circumference. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Draw circle r=5 cm. Keep compass span 5 cm, place needle on boundary and swing arcs through center to boundary.
(b) Since compass span equals radius 5 cm, every arc endpoint is exactly 5 cm from center, placing tips on circumference.

questions.question_text: If diameter of a circle is 21 cm, its radius is:
Set-square is primarily used to construct:
Draw a line segment PQ = 8.4 cm and divide it into two equal halves by construction.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Construct perpendicular bisector of PQ. Intersection point M divides PQ into PM = MQ = 4.2 cm.

questions.question_text: Find perimeter of a rectangle constructed with sides 7.5 cm and 3.5 cm.
Construct an equilateral triangle of side 5 cm using ruler and compass.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Draw base AB = 5 cm. Set compass span 5 cm. Draw arcs from A and B to intersect at C. Join AC and BC.

questions.question_text: Describe how to check accuracy of a drawn right angle without a protractor.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Use 3-4-5 Pythagorean triangle method or superimpose a standard 90° set-square corner over the angle.

questions.question_text:
Case Study: Circular Park Track Design. A circular park of radius 20 m has a concentric running track of width 5 m around its outer edge.
(a) Find radius of inner park and outer boundary. (2 marks)
(b) Construct a scaled model drawing on paper choosing scale 1 cm = 5 m. (3 marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Inner radius r1 = 20 m. Outer radius r2 = 20 + 5 = 25 m.
(b) Scaled inner radius = 20/5 = 4 cm. Scaled outer radius = 25/5 = 5 cm. Draw concentric circles of 4 cm and 5 cm on paper.

Assertion (A): Diameter is longest chord of a circle.
Reason (R): Diameter passes through center O and equals 2r.
options: A. Both A and R true, R explains A.
B. Both true, R doesn't explain.
questions.correct_answer: A. Both A and R true, R explains A.

questions.question_text: Write 3 construction steps for circle of radius 3.5 cm.
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: Mark center O, set compass 3.5 cm, rotate needle 360°. [2 Marks]

questions.question_text: How do you construct two concentric circles of radii 3 cm and 5 cm?
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: Mark center O, draw circle r=3 cm, draw second circle r=5 cm from same O. [2 Marks]

questions.question_text: Construct rectangle ABCD with AB = 6 cm and BC = 4 cm using set-square.
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: Draw base 6 cm, draw perpendiculars at endpoints of height 4 cm, join tops. [2 Marks]

questions.question_text: If diameter of circle is 14 cm, find its radius.
Can a chord of a circle be longer than its diameter? Explain.
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme: No! Diameter is the longest possible chord in any circle. [2 Marks]

questions.question_text:
(a) Explain how to construct a square of side 5 cm using ruler and set-square. (2 Marks)
(b) Verify that both diagonals of this square are equal. (2 Marks)
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme:
(a) Draw base 5 cm, erect 90° perpendiculars at both ends of length 5 cm, join top. [2 Marks]
(b) Measure diagonals with compass; both measure sqrt(50) = 7.07 cm. Equal! [2 Marks]

questions.question_text:
(a) Draw segment AB = 7 cm and copy its length to new line segment CD using compass. (2 Marks)
(b) Explain why compass transfer is more accurate than ruler tick alignment. (2 Marks)
questions.solution_and_marking_scheme:
(a) Lock compass span on AB, pivot on C to mark D. [2 Marks]
(b) Prevents visual alignment errors and ruler tick spacing discrepancies. [2 Marks]

questions.case_scenario_text:
Case Study: Regular Hexagon Inscription.
A student constructs a regular hexagon inside a circle of radius 4 cm using compass radius steps.

sub_questions.question_text: What compass opening is used to step around the boundary?
How many equal arc steps are formed on the circumference?
Find side length and total perimeter of the inscribed regular hexagon.
sub_questions.solution_and_marking_scheme:
Side length = radius = 4 cm. [1.5 Marks]
Perimeter = 6 x 4 = 24 cm. [1.5 Marks]
